title: Barsotti--Chevalley decomposition over an algebraically closed field
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure] and let $H/k$ be a smooth connected separated group scheme of finite type [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], not necessarily commutative. There exist a smooth connected affine $k$-group scheme $L$ of finite type, a closed normal subgroup inclusion $a:L\hookrightarrow H$ [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup], an abelian variety $C/k$ [def-sc-abelian-variety], and a homomorphism $p:H\to C$ such that $a$ identifies $L$ with the scheme-theoretic kernel of $p$ and $p$ is locally surjective for the big fppf topology [def-pc-fppf-site]. Here affine means isomorphic to the spectrum of a commutative ring [def-pc-scheme]. The trivial group and zero-dimensional abelian variety are allowed.

source.place: Theorem 8.27 and Note 8.30, printed pp.154--155; quotient map of Theorem 5.14 and Propositions 5.24--5.25, printed pp.102,104--105. Smoothness of the affine subgroup is part of the group-variety assertion over a perfect field. Algebraically closed specialization; fppf exactness is also explained in Conrad Definition 2.2. No Stacks tag states the Barsotti--Chevalley theorem.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-affine-normal-subgroup-products] to the ambient group $H$. The dimensions of its smooth connected affine closed normal subgroups form a nonempty subset of $\{0,\ldots,\dim H\}$: the identity subgroup $1=\operatorname{Spec}k$ is one such subgroup. Choose $L$ with greatest dimension, and let $a:L\hookrightarrow H$ be its inclusion. This already gives smoothness, connectedness, affineness, finite type and closed normality of $L$.

source.place: Proposition 8.2 and Proposition 6.42, printed pp.149,134: greatest-dimension choice.

proof.text: If $M\subseteq H$ is any other smooth connected affine closed normal subgroup, [lem-sfb-affine-normal-subgroup-products] gives such a subgroup $P=LM$ containing $L$ and $M$. A strict inclusion $L\subsetneq P$ would give $\dim L<\dim P$, contrary to the choice of $L$. Thus $P=L$ and $M\subseteq L$. In particular $L$ is the largest subgroup with the stated properties.

source.place: Proposition 8.2 through Lemma 6.41 and Proposition 6.42, printed pp.149,134.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-affine-normal-quotient-lifts] to $(H,L)$. Obtain a smooth connected separated finite-type group scheme $Q$ and a smooth surjective homomorphism $p:H\to Q$ of finite presentation with scheme-theoretic kernel $L$. The lemma applies because step 1 gave every hypothesis on $L$; no commutativity or affineness of $H$ is required.

source.place: Theorem 5.14, Propositions 5.24--5.25, Corollary 5.26 and Proposition 1.62; printed pp.102,104--105,24.

proof.text: Let $S\subseteq Q$ be a smooth connected affine closed normal subgroup. By [lem-sfb-smooth-affine-normal-quotient-lifts], its inverse image $P=H\times_Q S$ is a smooth connected affine closed normal subgroup of $H$ containing $L$, and $P\to S$ has kernel $L$. Step 2 gives $P=L$. For any $s:T\to S$, pull back $p$ along $T\to S\hookrightarrow Q$. The resulting $u:U\to T$ is flat, surjective and finitely presented by the same lemma. It is fpqc [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]: for an affine open $V\subseteq T$, quasi-compactness gives a finite affine cover of $u^{-1}(V)$, whose images cover $V$. Its lift to $P=L$ shows that $s\circ u$ is the identity section. By uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent], $s$ is the identity section. Taking $T=S$ and $s=\mathrm{id}_S$ yields $e_S\circ(S\to\operatorname{Spec}k)=\mathrm{id}_S$; the reverse composite is the identity of $\operatorname{Spec}k$. Hence $S$ is trivial.

source.place: Proposition 8.2 last sentence, printed p.149; Theorem 5.55, p.113. Local equality uses representable fpqc descent, Stacks Tag 023Q, descent.tex, lemma-fpqc-universal-effective-epimorphisms.

proof.text: Step 4 verifies exactly the no-affine-normal-subgroup hypothesis of [lem-sfb-pseudoabelian-proper-algclosed] for $Q$; the other hypotheses hold by step 3 and the field hypothesis of the item. Hence $Q$ is proper. Put $C=Q$. By [def-sc-abelian-variety], properness, smoothness and connectedness are precisely the required abelian-variety properties. In particular no extra commutativity hypothesis has been used.

source.place: Theorems 8.26--8.27, printed pp.154--155; definition of complete group variety.

proof.text: For a $k$-scheme $T$ and a point $x:T\to C$, [lem-sfb-smooth-affine-normal-quotient-lifts] says that $H\times_C T\to T$ is flat, surjective and locally of finite presentation, hence is an fppf covering. Its first projection is a lift of $x$ to $H$ over that covering. This proves local surjectivity of $p$ in the big fppf topology. The kernel identification and inclusion are those of step 3, so $(L,a,C,p)$ has every property in the statement. The argument used no positive-dimension requirement on either $L$ or $C$, and includes the trivial group.

source.place: Propositions 5.24--5.25 and Corollary 5.27, printed pp.104--105; fppf interpretation of the quotient morphism.

proof_origin.place: Theorem 8.27, proof on printed p.155 via Proposition 8.2 (p.149), Lemma 6.41 and Proposition 6.42 (p.134), Theorem 8.26 (p.154), and quotient theory of Chapter 5.
